headline: Park Pass and Backcountry Reservation Requirements
reservation: Entry requires a valid Parks Canada pass, while overnight stays in the backcountry or at Jeremy's Bay require separate reservations. These systems open months in advance and typically reach capacity for summer weekends immediately. Check the Parks Canada official site for specific opening dates and mandatory orientation requirements for paddlers.

days.title: Inland Waters and Heritage

stops.name: Kejimkujik Lake
stops.detail: The park's namesake waterbody, ideal for viewing the Mi'kmaw cultural landscape from a canoe.

stops.name: Mill Falls
stops.detail: A short walk to see the Mersey River's dark, tannin-rich waters cascading over granite ledges.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes from Caledonia; interior roads are paved but slow.
days.note: Water levels in the Mersey River can vary; check local conditions for paddling safety.

days.title: Old Growth and Glacial Trails

stops.name: Hemlocks and Hardwoods Trail
stops.detail: A boardwalk path through a rare stand of ancient eastern hemlocks.

stops.name: Big Rocks
stops.detail: An impressive collection of glacial erratics that demonstrate the region's geological history.

days.driving: Minimal driving within the park; allow 15 minutes between trailheads.
days.note: Trail conditions may be wet; boardwalks can be slippery after rain.

days.title: Seaside Adjunct Exploration

stops.name: Port Joli Sector
stops.detail: Explore the rugged Atlantic coastline, distinct from the inland forest ecosystem.

stops.name: St. Catherines River Beach
stops.detail: A coastal hike offering opportunities to spot harbor seals on offshore ledges.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours between the Inland and Seaside sectors; they are not connected by park roads.
days.note: The Seaside adjunct is a separate geographic location on the coast; plan travel time accordingly.

intel.title: Visitor Center Capacity
intel.text: The main Visitor Centre lot is the primary hub for information and permits. During peak summer weeks, secondary lots at trailheads may fill by midday.

intel.title: Inland Connectivity
intel.text: Expect limited to no cell service in the backcountry interior. Public Wi-Fi is generally restricted to the Visitor Centre area.

intel.title: Gateway Gas
intel.text: Caledonia and Liverpool are the primary fueling stations for the Inland and Seaside sectors respectively. No fuel services are provided within federal park boundaries.

intel.title: Dark Sky Preservation
intel.text: As a Dark Sky Preserve, night sky viewing is a priority. Suggested times for stargazing depend on lunar cycles and clear weather windows.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: Portions of the park roads may be closed or unmaintained during the winter season. Check the official Parks Canada status report for spring opening dates.

plan.arrival: Pick up a rental in Halifax and stock up on groceries in Bridgewater or Liverpool. Ensure you have your Parks Canada confirmation ready for the gatehouse.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for the main loop; however, the Seaside adjunct access road is narrower and requires careful driving.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset at Kejimkujik Lake offers expansive views of the water, with the best colors typically appearing in late summer.
